newsitem.title: ITALY: Generali revises net gain from Axa sale.
newsitem.headline: Generali revises net gain from Axa sale.

text.p: Italian insurance group Generali on Tuesday revised the capital gain given in its 1996 result statement on Monday from the sale of its stake in French insurer Axa SA.

A Generali statement on Tuesday said without the proceeds from the sale of Generali's stake in Axa, group consolidated profits for 1996 would have been 800 billion lire, and not the 880 billion lire given in a Generali statement on Monday.
All other details were correct when Generali said on Monday that its net consolidated attributable profit in 1996 rose to 1.437 trillion lire from 695 billion lire in 1995.
Axa finalised its merger with UAP on Monday.

The parent company announced an unchanged dividend per ordinary share of 375 lire for 1996, which taking into account a free capital issue, saw the total company's dividend payout increase 10 percent.

The group said that 1996 overall premiums rose 10.7 percent to 34.924 trillion lire, of which some 30.1 percent came from the Italian market. Group investments rose 15 percent to 121.700 trillion lire.
Generali said that its group operating result in 1996 was 1.187 trillion lire after 1.041 trillion lire in 1995.
At the parent company level, net profits in 1997 rose to 519.7 billion lire, some 37 billion lire above 1995.
Generali shares were marked up 2.16 percent at 30,400 lire and Alleanza shares were 3.35 percent firmer at 12,180 lire in a slightly firmer Milan stock market at 1020 GMT.
On Monday, Italian life insurance company Alleanza Assicurazioni said its 1996 net consolidate income rose 60 percent to 246.7 billion lire from 1995's figure of 154.2 billion lire.
Alleanza is Italy's largest life insurer for individual policies with a market share in Italy of 11.7 percent, and the group is 64 percent controlled by Generali.
